description: <attemptDir>/attempt-intent.json. The controller writes it right after it takes the attempt lock, before its first await, and replaces it atomically while it holds the lock (a resumed attempt that never got an envelope carries the intent of its new launch). It holds what the adopt door needs to close the attempt if the controller dies before it writes envelope.json: the lock is free, no envelope exists, the intent is valid. Adopt then publishes an envelope from it (envelope.v3.json origin adopt-not-started), a start refusal with code no-envelope, and goes on as for any attempt that was never bound (receipt abandoned-not-started, the steps, closed.json). A controller that settles the run without a launch (refused, or already answered) removes it. No secrets. A directory with controller/commands (the pre-supervisor launch record) is never closed from an intent.

fields.attemptId: string, the id the envelope of this launch would carry
fields.runDir: absolute path of the attempt directory; adopt accepts the intent only when it names the directory it was found in

mode.meaning: what the controller would have launched. The adopt-written envelope is always direct: no agent of a not-started attempt runs in a pane

fields.cwd: absolute working directory of the agent
fields.steps: array of process step items exactly as envelope.v3.json `steps.item` (settle-attempt, finalize-home, and cleanup-trust for a terminal attempt); never the release-slot builtin: adopt adds it when the intent has `terminal`. Built by the same function that builds the envelope's steps. The first one names hostBin and payloadRoot, which become the envelope's
fields.terminal: object {slot: {key, groupKey}, endpointEnv}, optional; only with mode terminal. The controller replaces the intent with this field right before it allocates the attempt's pane, so a controller killed from then on leaves the pane's key. slot.key equals attemptId (an intent whose key differs is invalid); endpointEnv holds only FGOS_HERDR_* and HERDR_* string values (the herdr endpoint, no secrets). Adopt copies slot into the envelope it publishes, appends the release-slot builtin to its steps and records the endpoint as terminal-endpoint.json, so the pane is released by its key
fields.sideFile: absolute path of the side file the envelope would name (it does not exist for a not-started attempt)

invariants: written under the attempt lock, so a reader that finds the lock free and the file present has a complete file
its absence with a lock and no envelope reads legacy-run: nothing is closed from a directory without one
